scope: Original geometric proposals and empty physical-evidence forms; no authored lesson or sample.

sourceBasis.mode: earlier exact reviewed receipts retained; no fresh source retrieval or source-media inspection in this preparation
sourceBasis.boundary: Earlier source reading distinguishes overlap, layers, tension and limited running-stitch uses. These original schematics do not reproduce a source design or prove an attachment. Earlier rights and physical-review limits remain.

coordinates.units: dimensionless schematic units, not centimetres, stitch spacing or material dimensions
coordinates.punctureMeaning: Proposed through-locations only. Dashed joining lines indicate ordering, not needle motion or an over/under thread path. All points are away from boundaries.
coordinates.crossSectionMeaning: Presence of intended layers at location 1; drawn thickness/gap is arbitrary, not material or assembly guidance.

plans.label: Full cover; proposed locations meet both layers
Full cover; proposed locations miss the base
Incomplete cover; marked locations meet both layers

interpretationLimits: Coverage is a planar overlap calculation, not a physical repair pass.
Passing both drawing predicates does not show that thread is fastened, tension is suitable, edges resist fraying or the sample survives use/washing.
The partial-cover plan deliberately leaves the right half of the hole uncovered and has an open proposed path; it isolates a coverage question, not a single-variable durability experiment.
The missing-base plan locates every proposed through-location over the hole. Its local cross-section depicts a gap, not fabric magically remaining beneath the hole.

reviewCards.question: Choose the actual material/sample and limited attachment claim; exclude safety-critical or durable-repair claims absent appropriate testing.
Specify and review stitch type, spacing, intended layers, start/end fastening, tension, tools and handling before any practical instructions are authored.
Agree the sample inspection and second-person reproduction protocol, deviations and failure reporting. Distinguish a drawing predicate from a physical observation.
Review non-sewing analysis and optional making access routes; identify exact sample images, descriptions, permissions and release scope.
reviewCards.requires: practitioner/access reviewer and actual asset permissions

activities.task: Compare coverage and layer presence separately. State which facts the drawing establishes and which require a specimen.
Use location 1 and the cross-section to explain whether base material is present; do not infer a real finished stitch.
Name the additional fastening, material, inspection and reproduction evidence needed before calling this a successful attachment.

rights: Original diagrams and original prose; no source figures, photographs, handouts or patterns copied. Public release terms are not granted by this packet.
remaining: Practical construction/protocol review, real specimen and second-person reproduction, applicable access/learner observations, final artifact review, capacity and release.
